raw.thesis: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies, designed to observe work patterns, identify AI automation opportunities, and automatically deploy and monitor AI agents. Its core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an Observe Layer that captures work patterns, an Intelligence Layer that understands employee intent and business value, and an Execution Layer that builds and manages AI agents. This system focuses on understanding the "Work Graph" to pinpoint inefficiencies and strategically deploy AI where it can provide the most impact. It aims to offer a "Continuous AI lift" by constantly adapting and deploying agents. The venture is positioned to assist AI-first companies struggling with measuring AI savings, unreliable ROI, and system drift. This venture is for AI-first companies and enterprises who want to deploy AI automation at scale. The founder's immediate goal for this venture is not explicitly stated, but the description points towards building a growth startup in the AI automation space. Based on the description, the venture appears to be at the concept or idea stage, with the architecture and vision clearly defined but no mention of development or user acquisition.
raw.product_description: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" with a three-layered architecture. Layer 1 (Observe) uses lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns, application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation. Layer 2 (Intelligence) acts as a "Brain" to detect employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift." Layer 3 (Execution) is an "Agent Factory" that automates the generation, deployment, and monitoring of AI agents for high-ROI opportunities, complete with approval gates. The system leverages existing foundation models and focuses on the "Work Graph" to identify areas for AI assistance and continuous improvement.
raw.evidence_of_stage: The venture describes a detailed architecture and vision but provides no evidence of a built product, users, or revenue.
raw.core_excitement: narma is excited about the prospect of a single system that can observe work, decide what AI should do, and continuously build and deploy AI agents for a "Continuous AI lift." The unique insight is the opportunity to automate AI deployment by focusing on the "Work Graph" to address telemetry, ROI, and drift challenges.
